title: Converting Degrees and Radians
trouble: Students multiply by the wrong factor and get answers like 30° = 5400/π.

blocks.html: You now have two units for angles. Both describe a half turn: it is $180^\circ$ and it is $\pi$ radians (half of $2\pi$). That one fact is all you need to convert, as in radian measure.
$$180^\circ = \pi \text{ radians}.$$ Degrees to radians: multiply by $\dfrac{\pi}{180^\circ}$. Radians to degrees: multiply by $\dfrac{180^\circ}{\pi}$.

Since $180^\circ$ and $\pi$ radians are the same angle, the fraction $\frac{\pi}{180^\circ}$ equals $1$, and multiplying by $1$ never changes an amount. You only pick the version of $1$ that cancels the unit you have, the way you convert inches to feet.

blocks.title: Degrees to radians
steps: Multiply by $\dfrac{\pi}{180^\circ}$ so the degrees cancel: $135^\circ \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{180^\circ} = \dfrac{135\pi}{180}$.
Simplify the fraction: $135$ and $180$ share a factor of $45$, so $\dfrac{135\pi}{180} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.

blocks.title: No $\pi$ in sight
steps: That is about $114.6^\circ$, a bit more than a right angle.

blocks.html: Multiplying by the wrong factor, for example $30^\circ \cdot \frac{180}{\pi} = \frac{5400}{\pi}$. Check the units: the unit you start with must cancel, so degrees go in the denominator when you convert to radians. Check the size too: a radian is about $57^\circ$, so the radian number is always much smaller than the degree number.
